summary: Thousand Palms sprawls across 23.6 square miles of flat Coachella Valley desert floor yet holds fewer than 8,000 residents, giving it a population density of just 325 per square mile — roughly one-tenth the density of neighboring Palm Springs, which means long sight lines to the San Jacinto and Little San Bernardino mountain ranges bracket almost every view. The Coachella Valley Preserve, a federally protected habitat for the Coachella Valley fringe-toed lizard, sits at the community's northern edge, offering miles of sandy trails through palm oases and mesquite hummocks — genuine desert wilderness accessible by a short drive from most homes. With an average daytime high of 84°F and nearly 11 hours of sunshine year-round, summer heat is the defining trade-off: triple-digit days from June through September are routine, and outdoor life migrates to early morning or evening. A median home value of $260,500 against a median household income of $80,280 yields a price-to-income ratio around 3.2 — notably affordable by California standards — though the local economy leans heavily on service and hospitality sectors tied to the broader Coachella Valley, so most employment means commuting west on Interstate 10 toward Palm Desert or beyond. Thousand Palms is, at its core, a low-density desert outpost where affordable housing and dramatic landscape coexist with the reality that nearly everything — jobs, dining variety, major retail — lives a car ride away.
